newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-McIntosh agrees to Merrill offer.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-McIntosh agrees to Merrill offer.

text.p: Brokerage firm McIntosh Securities Ltd said on Tuesday it had agreed to a A$1.40 per share takeover bid by Merrill Lynch and Co Inc, valuing the company at about A$117 million.
The offer represents a premium of about 48 percent on McIntosh's average closing price in the last 30 days. It also represents 11.1 times pre-tax profits and 1.3 times net assets.
McIntosh shares last traded at A$1.25 on Friday, prior to the company requesting a trading halt on Monday and suspension on Tuesday morning ahead of the mooted takeover announcement.
McIntosh said its directors unanimously recommended that shareholders accept the Merrill offer and they would accept for their own shares.
The bid was subject to 90 percent share acceptances and U.S. and local regulatory approvals, among other things.

A joint statement said the combined firm would be known as Merrill Lynch (Australia) Pty Ltd and would be one of the leading financial services firms in Australasia, with leading positions in equity origination, sales, trading and research, as well as in debt origination, sales and trading, cross-border investment banking, private client and private banking.
The firm would also be a leading underwriter of both equity and debt securities for corporations and governments in Australia and New Zealand, and a leading trader in these markets, it said.

The combined firm would be headed by co-chief executives Gregory Bundy and John Magowan. Bundy is currently managing director, international equity sales and trading at Merrill Lynch in New York and would relocate to Melbourne. Magowan is currently chief executive officer-stockbroking, at McIntosh.

McIntosh managing director Bruce Parncutt would be offered the position of senior vice president, Merrill Lynch International, if the bid was successful, while chairman and McIntosh founder John McIntosh would be offered the position of senior adviser to the new local firm.
Merrill Lynch said the bid would be funded by existing cash resources.

"This is a very strategic fit for us in Australia, and reflects our continuing effort to bring to bear unmatched resources, market presence and market intelligence on behalf of all our clients - including institutions, corporations, governments and individual investors worldwide," Merrill chairman and chief executive Daniel Tully said.
